subject: Mathematics
questionText: Let $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = \hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, and $\vec{c} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$. Which of the following vectors is/are perpendicular to both $\vec{a} + \vec{b}$ and $\vec{b} + \vec{c}$?
solution:
$\vec{a} + \vec{b} = 2\hat{i} + 2\hat{k}$, $\vec{b} + \vec{c} = 2\hat{i}$.
Their cross product $(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) \times (\vec{b}+\vec{c}) = (2\hat{i}+2\hat{k}) \times 2\hat{i} = 4(\hat{k} \times \hat{i}) = 4\hat{j}$.
Any vector along $\hat{j}$ direction (e.g. $\hat{j}, 2\hat{j}, -4\hat{j}$) is perpendicular to both.
